This couple came after two unsuccessful donor IUI cycles, facing challenges on both sides: poor ovarian reserve and zero sperm count.
A detailed evaluation revealed obstructive azoospermia. Through TESA, motile sperm was successfully retrieved and cryopreserved, enabling IVF with ICSI treatment planning.
The outcome: a confirmed clinical pregnancy and the birth of two healthy baby girls.
Every case has a story. The right diagnosis can make all the difference. 💕

A couple with a 7-year history of infertility faced an unexpected hurdle on the day of egg retrieval. While 18 mature eggs were successfully retrieved, no viable sperm was available for fertilisation.

Tracking your menstrual cycle is a simple habit that can provide valuable insights into your overall reproductive and hormonal health. Noting the start and end dates of your periods, cycle length, flow pattern, and associated symptoms can help you better understand your body's natural rhythm. It may also help identify changes such as irregular periods, missed cycles, unusually heavy bleeding, or increased menstrual discomfort.

Cycle tracking can be done using a calendar, diary, or mobile app and may support more informed discussions with healthcare professionals when needed. Factors such as stress, lifestyle changes, sleep patterns, nutrition, and hormonal fluctuations can all influence the menstrual cycle.

Being aware of your cycle is not about predicting dates alone—it is about understanding patterns and recognizing when something may need further attention. Small observations today can contribute to better awareness of women's health over time.

PCOS and PCOD are common hormonal conditions that can affect menstrual health, metabolism, skin, hair, and reproductive wellness. While irregular periods are often one of the most recognized symptoms, women may also experience acne, weight changes, hair thinning, excessive hair growth, mood fluctuations, and challenges related to fertility. The effects of PCOS and PCOD can vary significantly from one individual to another.

At a **PCOS/PCOD Clinic in Dadar**, understanding the underlying factors contributing to hormonal imbalance is an important part of overall health awareness. Healthy lifestyle habits such as balanced nutrition, regular exercise, adequate sleep, and stress management can support hormonal wellness and general well-being.

Monitoring menstrual health and seeking timely evaluation when symptoms persist can help women better understand their reproductive health and make informed decisions about long-term wellness.

PCOS is a common hormonal condition that can affect many aspects of a woman’s health beyond irregular periods.
